transcript.finalText:
he skipped test checks a file the tool isn't allowed to read (expecting `cannot read`). It can't work when running as root, so that error has no test that actually ran.

**Files, all at the project root:**
- `jsonpatch.mjs` – the library, exporting `parsePointer`, `applyPatch` and `PatchError`. Copying and comparing documents use loops rather than recursion, so very deeply nested results can't overflow the stack.
- `jsonpatch-cli.mjs` – the command-line tool. It never reads a file past 1,048,577 bytes, so oversized input is reported as `too large` straight away. Standard input is only read when it is needed, after the patch has passed all its checks.
- `test/jsonpatch.test.mjs` and `test/cli.test.mjs` – tests using `node:test`.
- `package.json` (`"type": "module"`, and `npm test` runs `node --test "test/*.test.mjs"`) and a `README.md` with usage and exit codes.

**Review:** no specialist sections were needed for work this size, so I built it myself. The reviewer gave it 8/10, a pass. After that I rewrote one deep-nesting test that took about 40 seconds; the whole suite now runs in about 1.2 seconds.

**Possible next steps:**
- An error the spec doesn't cover in the command-line tool currently prints a Node stack trace instead of one `Error:` line. An example is a broken output pipe when output goes to a command that exits early.
- Share the step that finds the parent between `add` and `replace`.

The summary is saved in `.team/reports/2026-11-03/011232-supervisor-summary.md`.
